title: Frequently asked questions
subtitle: Quick guide for coordinators, team leads, and field crews.

how_it_works.title: How WinProx works
how_it_works.intro: A simple workflow to manage sites, issues, and internal teams.
how_it_works.summary: Workflow: sites and units, QR issues, tasks for internal teams, follow-up via dashboard, briefing, and calendar.

steps.title: Create a site
steps.text: Start by creating a site. Add units (machines, zones, or areas) with a short description or location hint so issues and tasks link correctly.

steps.title: Create an issue
steps.text: Create an issue yourself or let reporters submit via QR code, optionally with photos. Everything stays in one place.

steps.title: Add updates
steps.text: Add extra information or photos so coordinators and crews see the same picture.

steps.title: Update status
steps.text: Show what happens with the issue: new, in progress, done, or closed.

steps.title: Task for an internal team
steps.text: For a unit issue, a task is created automatically for the linked team. You can also assign tasks manually or schedule recurring maintenance (for example monthly) via the calendar.

steps.title: Field worker registration via team QR
steps.text: Field workers scan the team QR and start or complete tasks on site.
steps.highlight: Field workers use the team QR without a WinProx login.

steps.title: Follow up and close
steps.text: Coordinators track tasks in the dashboard, briefing, and calendar. Mark completed when work is done.

how_it_works.box_body: Organise maintenance crews by team. Link teams to units so issues land on the right list automatically. Via the team QR, field workers log updates and photos on site.

pricing.title: How much does WinProx cost?
pricing.intro: WinProx starts with a trial period. After that, choose a plan based on the number of units at your sites (machines, zones, or areas). Activate under Subscription. Limits for units, documents, and announcements apply to your whole organisation.
pricing.summary: Trial period, then Micro, Starter, Pro, Business, or Enterprise. Documents and announcements have per-unit and per-organisation limits.
pricing.content_note: Announcements: only active, non-expired messages count (per linked unit). Documents: every stored file counts for your organisation, including deactivated ones — delete to free space. During the trial, your organisation may upload up to 10 documents.

micro.documents: Up to 2 documents per unit · max. 10 for your organisation
micro.description: Ideal for small businesses and compact property managers.

starter.documents: Up to 4 documents per unit · max. 20 for your organisation
starter.description: Ideal for a single site or pilot with a compact coordination team.

pro.documents: Up to 6 documents per unit · max. 40 for your organisation
pro.description: Suited for growing facility organisations with more units and internal teams.

business.documents: Up to 8 documents per unit · max. 80 for your organisation
business.description: For organisations with multiple sites, many units, and larger teams. Includes API access and webhooks.

enterprise.units: For large site operators and complex portfolios. Contact us.
enterprise.description: Includes API access, webhooks, and custom solutions.

qr_code.title: How do the QR codes work?
qr_code.body: There are two QR codes: the unit QR for reporters (new issue, open issues, optional documents and announcements) and the team QR for field workers (start tasks, photos, and status on site). Print both visibly. Scanning opens the right portal in the browser — no app install.
qr_code.summary: Unit QR for reporters and team QR for field workers; both work in the browser without an app.

reporter_portal.title: How does the reporter portal work?
reporter_portal.intro: After scanning the unit QR, a simple web page opens for that unit. Reporters submit problems; field workers linked to the team can also complete open tasks for that unit there.
reporter_portal.summary: After scanning the unit QR: report issues, open issues, documents, announcements, and optional on-site tasks.

sections.title: New issue
sections.text: Report a problem quickly with category, description, and optional photos. The issue links to the correct unit.

sections.title: Open issues
sections.text: Overview of active issues for this unit, with detail and status.

sections.title: Documents
sections.text: View documents your organisation shared for the site or unit, when available.

sections.title: Announcements
sections.text: Read announcements meant for reporters or teams on this site.

sections.title: On-site tasks (field workers)
sections.text: Field workers who open the unit QR and belong to the linked team see open tasks for that unit. They can start tasks, add photos, and complete them — the same flow as via the team QR.

for_who.title: Who is WinProx for?
for_who.body: WinProx helps factories, hospitals, municipalities, and large site operators centralise issues, internal teams, and field follow-up.
for_who.summary: For facility organisations that centralise issues, teams, and field work.

user_roles.title: How do user roles work?
user_roles.summary: Administrator: full control and subscription. Standard user: daily follow-up without user management. Worker: tasks on location via team-QR without login.

roles.title: Administrator
roles.text: Has full control over WinProx and is the only role that can add or remove users. Also manages subscription and user settings.

roles.title: Standard user
roles.text: Handles daily follow-up: sites, issues, and tasks. No access to colleague accounts or subscription settings.

roles.title: Worker (team)
roles.text: Uses the team-QR to start tasks on location, add photos, and complete tasks. Works without WinProx login — registration happens via the team-QR.

data_export.title: Can I export my data?
data_export.body: Yes. At the bottom of the Users page, an administrator can download a JSON export with account and activity data in your environment (sites, issues, tasks). Keep the file secure and do not share it unnecessarily.
data_export.summary: Administrators can download a JSON export of account and activity data under Users.

internal_teams.title: How do I set up internal teams?
internal_teams.body: Create teams via the Team menu. Link teams to units so issues and tasks route to the right group automatically.
internal_teams.summary: Create teams via Team and link them to units.

team_follow_up.title: How do internal teams follow up on tasks?
team_follow_up.body: Tasks appear on the team QR and in the dashboard. Workers handle tasks on site, add a description, and take photos when needed. Coordinators follow progress via the morning briefing and calendar.
team_follow_up.summary: Tasks via team QR and dashboard; follow-up via briefing and calendar.

multiple_locations.title: Can I manage multiple sites?
multiple_locations.body: Yes. You can follow multiple sites and units in one place and keep overview per site, issue, and task.
multiple_locations.summary: Multiple sites and units can be managed centrally.

mobile.title: Does WinProx work on smartphones?
mobile.body: Yes. WinProx runs fully in the browser on phone, tablet, and desktop. Field workers use the team QR on their phone.
mobile.summary: WinProx works in the browser on phone, tablet, and desktop.

install.title: Do I need to install software?
install.body: No. WinProx is a web application. Coordinators and field teams start immediately in the browser without a separate install.
install.summary: No install needed — everything runs in the browser.

status_help.title: Where can I find help about statuses?
status_help.body: On mobile, use the "Status help" button to read what each status means. On desktop, you see a description when you hover over the status.
status_help.summary: Status help on issues and tasks explains each status and the recommended next step.

dynamic_qr_codes.title: Dynamic QR codes
dynamic_qr_codes.body: WinProx supports two types of QR stickers: dynamic QR codes and static QR codes. Dynamic QR codes can be linked to a different unit at any time (re-linkable). Static QR codes are fixed to one specific unit. Print dynamic stickers in bulk. Go on site, stick a sticker and scan it with your phone. You must be logged in, after which you can assign a unit to that QR code sticker.
dynamic_qr_codes.summary: Dynamic QR codes are re-linkable, static QR codes are fixed. Print dynamic stickers in bulk and assign a unit on site.

stickers.title: Which stickers can I use?
stickers.body: For printing, we recommend labels from Avery or Herma due to their quality and compatibility with standard printers. The correct A4 sheet types are indicated.
stickers.summary: Avery and Herma labels recommended for printing. Correct A4 sheet types indicated.

style.title: What is WinProx style and Custom portal style?
style.body: WinProx style determines how the app looks for administrators and staff (standard, dark, high res). Custom portal style is optional and adjusts background and button colors for the public portal that reporters and workers see after scanning a QR code. Configure both under Settings.
style.summary: WinProx style for the app, Custom portal style for the public portal (background and button colors).
